title: The legacy screen, endpoints and rights of RWB-E4-035 serve an officer's notice screen, not a customer's offer view
source: RWB-E4-035 sections Screen and states, Endpoints and Permission checks; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.14 (FEAT-COM-01); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10
description: The legacy story of FEAT-COM-01 names the screen SCR-33 Template approval with the states Draft, approved and withdrawn, and the two notice endpoints POST /cases/{caseId}/notices and GET /notices/{noticeId} with the Litigation rights C and R. None of those three serves the feature as it is written: SCR-33 shows a template to an officer, the two endpoints generate and read a notice, and the actor of the feature is the customer on LINE OA and on HOME.SCB (FSD P6 A2.14.2 and A2.14.3.3). No source gives the screens of the two customer channels, their states or their field lists, and the RBAC matrix of TSD P6 T6.1 holds only the Documents and the Litigation columns, so no right is stated for a customer-channel read of an offer.
evidence: RWB-E4-035: "| Screen | SCR-33 Template approval | States: Draft; approved; withdrawn |" and "| Litigation | C | RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE |" with endpoints /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices and /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId}. FSD P6 A2.14.2: integration points "LINE OA, HOME.SCB"; A2.14.3.3: "Customer (borrower) | Primary". TSD P6 T6.1 columns: Documents, Litigation only.
legacy_ref: RWB-E4-035 (sections Endpoints, Screen and states, Permission checks)
proposed: Record that the two notice endpoints and their Litigation rights stay with RWB-P6-E1052-APP and RWB-P6-E2021-APP, that SCR-33 stays with the template stories, and that the offer view of FEAT-COM-01 is served to LINE OA and HOME.SCB through gateway-bff from the two operations of RWB-P6-E4035-CON, with the capability area and right declared there; fix the channel screens in RWB-PLT-N001-CON when the edge stories are planned.

title: No offer-view operation exists in the P6 inventory and the plan declares no C row for the two reads the view needs
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1 and T8; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.14; split plan slices for RWB-P6-E4035-APP
description: The endpoint inventory of the TSD P6 names eleven operations and none of them shows an offer to a customer, so the two operations of this key are new and no source gives their request, their answer or their codes. The view also reads the offer of the case from S2 rwb-treatment and the customer and the contact point of a channel from P1 rwb-source-data, because FSD P6 v3 reads contact points from v_ace_contact plus contact_point_ext and Architecture v5 gives the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views to rwb-source-data alone; the plan declares C = [] for RWB-P6-E4035-APP, so neither read has a contract story to build against. TSD P6 T8 maps REQ-OCC-011 to FEAT-COM-01 as "Written one epic ahead" with no story and no test, so the key serves no requirement row either.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T-A.1: API-P6-001 to API-P6-011, none of them an offer view. TSD P6 v2 T8: "| REQ-OCC-011 | FEAT-COM-01 | Written one epic ahead | With the story |". Split plan slices RWB-P6-E4035-APP and RWB-P6-E4035-CON: "C": []. FSD P6 v3 change note: "contact points from v_ace_contact plus contact_point_ext"; Architecture v5 slide 8: "30 recovery.v_ace_* views (read only by rwb-source-data)".
proposed: Publish the two offer-view operations in RWB-P6-E4035-CON as new, build the app story against their fakes, and add the S2 and P1 contract stories to the C list when they are planned; until then record in the API file which published surface each read is faked from, and add the requirement row of FEAT-COM-01 to the P6 list with the story and its test.

title: The decision code of an offer view and the shape of the contact-stop picture are not stated by any source
source: RWB-E4-035 AC1 and AC2; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.14.3.1 (VR-P6-014-1, VR-P6-014-2); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-RES-09, R-SET-04, R-UNI-20, R-UNI-39); TSD P6 Communications v2 T3 and T5.3
description: Legacy AC1 requires that the system "writes the result to the decision log with the rule version", and R-RES-09 and R-SET-04 carry the route decision of an offer under the route sets D5, D6 and D6.4, but no source states the decision code of an offer view, so the record element is declared in RWB-P6-E4035-CON with the code left as a placeholder. The contact stop that VR-P6-014-1 acts on is a deviation fact of S8 and no source says how a service keeps that picture between events, so the local projection behind the two consumed deviation events is declared as a design of this service without a source shape.
evidence: RWB-E4-035 AC1: "Then the system writes the result to the decision log with the rule version". FSD P6 A2.14.3.1: "VR-P6-014-1 Contact attempted while a contact stop is in force | MSG-P6-001". Routing Logic v4: R-RES-09 decision codes "D5, D6" and R-SET-04 "D6.4"; no rule row names an offer view.
proposed: Declare the record element with the decision code, the rule id and the rule version, take the rule values from the offer on the treatment contract, carry the decision code as a placeholder until the owner of the decision types publishes it, and declare the contact-stop projection as internal state of rwb-comms fed by DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared.

title: No source fixes which offer fields a customer channel is shown or which contact-point fields prove consent
source: RWB-E4-035 section Data; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.14.3.2 field catalog; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 and T3.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10
description: The legacy data table of RWB-E4-035 lists six entities - v_ace_customer, treatment, notice, decision_log_entry, rule_row and template - and the FSD field catalog of A2.14 lists the eight notice fields only. Neither states which fields the customer sees on LINE or on the web, whether the offer amount and its validity date are shown, or which fields of a contact point prove consent for a channel; the legacy key also names a template field set whose body is a claim-check reference. The view resource is therefore fixed in RWB-P6-E4035-CON from the fields the module owns, and three of its elements stand as placeholders until the channel owners and the data steward name them.
evidence: RWB-E4-035 Data table: v_ace_customer, treatment, notice, decision_log_entry, rule_row, template. FSD P6 A2.14.3.2: notice.case_id to notice.sent_type. FSD P6 v3 change note: contact points from v_ace_contact plus contact_point_ext; no field list of a consent proof.
proposed: Close the OfferView field list in the RWB-P6-E4035-CON baseline review with the channel owners and the data steward, keep it to identifiers, codes, dates and one claim-check reference, and confirm with the rwb-source-data owner which contact-point fields prove consent for a channel before the app story is built.

title: No source gives the capability area or the right of an offer-view operation, and the legacy story names the Litigation rights of another surface
source: RWB-E4-035 section Permission checks; TSD P6 Communications v2 T6.1, T6.2 and T-A.1; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.14.3.3
description: The permission checks of the legacy story name the Litigation area with right C and right R for the two notice endpoints it borrowed, and those operations are built by the generation and dispatch stories of the module. The RBAC matrix of TSD P6 T6.1 holds only the Documents and the Litigation columns, and the endpoint inventory declares the rights of the eleven operations it holds, but no source gives a right for a read of an offer by a customer or for the record of a view, and no source gives the screen states of the two customer channels. RWB-P6-E4035-CON therefore declares the two operations as Treatment and offer, rights C and R, with the scope applied, and the declaration is the assumption of this gap.
evidence: RWB-E4-035 Permission checks: "| Litigation | C | RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE |" and "| Litigation | R | RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, ... |" for POST /cases/{caseId}/notices and GET /notices/{noticeId}. TSD P6 T6.1 columns: Documents, Litigation. T-A.1 declares rights for API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 only.
legacy_ref: RWB-E4-035 (sections Permission checks, Screen and states)
proposed: Confirm the capability area and right of the two offer-view operations with the rwb-access owner in the RWB-P6-E4035-CON baseline review, keep the scope applied on the case, and add the customer-channel screens and their masking to RWB-PLT-N001-CON when the edge stories are planned.

title: The two contracts and the contact-stop events the view depends on carry no C row and no source shape in this key's plan
source: Split plan slices for RWB-P6-E4035-APP and RWB-P6-E4035-CON; TSD P6 Communications v2 T5.3 appendix; Ownership Map v1 (treatment owner S2, deviation owner S8, contact_point_ext owner P1)
description: The view read of S2 rwb-treatment and the party and contact-point read of P1 rwb-source-data are real reads of the app story, and the contact stop arrives on the two deviation events of S8, but the plan declares C = [] and I = [] for both slices of this key and names no S2, P1 or S8 contract or integration story. The two contracts, their fakes and the field types of an offer are therefore declared from the published documents and the Ownership Map only, and the drift test of RWB-P6-E4035-CON holds them until the owners publish their own baselines.
evidence: Split plan: RWB-P6-E4035-APP "C": [], "I": [], "H": [RWB-P6-E4035-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON]. TSD P6 v2 T5.3: NoticeGenerated, NoticeDispatched, NoticeDelivered published only; no deviation event. RWB-P6-E2022-CON consumes rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1 and rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1 for the same conduct check.
proposed: Build the two reads and the two consumed events against fakes derived from the published contracts, add the S2 and P1 contract stories to the C list and the S8 event rows to the I list of the wave 3 integration story when they are planned, and keep the drift test as the guard until then.
